The DGA method applying Key Gas method and Duval Triangle method is used to identify such type of faults. The RadBas, Tan-Sigmoid, Log-sigmoid, Purelin linear transfer functions were chosen to find mean absolute error and least learning time during the analysis. The DGA results of 244 power transformers in distribution system were used as training data while additional DGA results of 100 power transformers were tested and compared to manual analysis. The results show that there is 6.4% absolute error from manual fault prediction. The method and tool are appropriate and less time consuming for condition-based maintenance of power transformer.

articleTitle: Thai Milled Rice Quality Classification Based on Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Rice is the most important food crop in Thailand for both domestic consumptions and export sections. Rice quality evaluation is a key process and a very big challenge for both research and the industry. Traditionally, rice grain physical quality inspection is done manually by the human inspector, but it is relative, time-consuming, varying results, and costly. Machine vision and deep learning techniques are the alternative solutions for automated, non-destructive analysis and cost-effective techniques. In this research, we propose an integration of an image processing-based system and deep learning approach for milled rice quality classification based on THAI AGRICULTURAL STANDARD. The two key challenges are the complexity of multiple criteria for the milled rice classification to meet the standard and small with a dense object in the real-world situation. To deal with this problem, we adopted Mask-RCNN, which is an instance segmentation framework, to perform three main tasks which are detection, segmentation, and classification. Experimental evaluation shows that our system achieves 0.96 mean average precision (mAP). The study results demonstrate that the proposed system provides capability and potential for rice quality classification to meet the standard. The system is compatible with touching kernels and dense object situations.

articleTitle: Magnetic TFET (MAG-TFET)
abstract: This paper presents a new structural magnetic field sensor device. The device structure uses the basic structure of tunneling field effect transistor (TFET). The mechanism uses the current-mode Hall phenomenon with tunneling electron carriers from source to drain. The device structure consists of source, gate and drain with two separate contacts on both sides D1 and D2 to accommodate the amount of current difference (∆I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>) caused by Lorentz’s force deflection. The study is carried out by using TCAD simulation. The magnetic field intensity response is linearly dependence. The sensitivity depends on the amount of current and magnetic field intensity. The sensitivity (S) obtained by this device which has width (F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>) 5 nm, length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>) 100 nm and height (F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>) 5 nm at biased current of 1000, 100, 10, 1 µA are 0.0133, 0.0263, 0.0812 and 1.22 µA.T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> respectively. From this experiment, the best relative sensitivity (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) is 0.000812 T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 100 µA.

articleTitle: Grounded Parallel RL, RC, and LC Immittance Simulators Using VDBAs and Passive Elements
abstract: This communication suggests a grounded parallel RL, RC, and LC immittance simulator. In this circuit, two voltage differencing buffered amplifiers (VDBAs) with two passive components are proposed. The VDBA device's transconductance gain can be used to electronically adjust the realized equivalent resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>), inductance (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>), and capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>), which is conditional on the choice of the passive element. The effect of the VDBA's non-idealities on the realized simulator is studied in this research. The second order voltage mode bandpass filter is realized using the proposed active LC parallel simulator, which is simulated using the PSPICE simulation program to ensure that it operates as desired.

articleTitle: A Development of Object Detection System based on Deep Learning Approach to Support the Laparoscope Manipulating Robot (LMR)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an object detection system based on the deep learning approach of computer vision to support the laparoscopic surgical robotic position control system. The system comprises two main phases, the training phase, and the real-time operating phase. In the training phase, a modified YOLOv4 algorithm is proposed to be adopted within the Darknet framework for training the weights of detection models. The best detection model is then selected to be assigned to the object detector in the real-time operating phase. The validation result of the detection model across the experiment datasets is 90% accuracy on average during the training phase. To validate the viability of real-time object detection, the proposed system was implemented in two test-cases of gynecologic surgery with the soft-body cadavers.

articleTitle: The Sharing of Similar Knowledge on Monte Carlo Algorithm applies to Cryptocurrency Trading Problem
abstract: Monte Carlo Algorithm is one of the various algorithms of Reinforcement Learning. It is used with problems that have finite states because of the memory problem. It must remember all the experiences to learn and make a decision. If the agent faces an unseen state, The Agent cannot use the experience for the decision to take the action. With these problems, we proposed the algorithm named The Sharing of Similar Knowledge on Monte Carlo Algorithm (SSKMC) to help Monte Carlo conducted with infinite states and leverage the old experience to decide the action when the agent faces a new experience (unseen state). In this paper, we tested the proposed algorithm with the Cryptocurrency Trading problem (Bitcoin) and compared the testing result of the proposed algorithm to Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). By the testing result of The Proposed algorithm makes net worth growth more than the DRL method by 1.55%.

articleTitle: An Improved RLS-based Interference Cancellation
abstract: An improved algorithm for mitigating the effect of power line interference in electrocardiogram (ECG) recording systems is presented. The proposed algorithm includes an interference detector (ID), an interference fundamental frequency estimator (IFFE), and an interference estimator (IE). The ID is used to evaluate the existence of the interference before recording. If it is present, the IFFE and IE are employed in the next steps. In the absence of interference, the observed signal is directly sent to the recorder and monitor. The presence of the ID can improve the performance of the system in terms of computational efficiency and system speed. The IFFE can track the variation of the interference frequency. Extensive computer simulations were run to demonstrate the performance of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Internet of Things Using Artificial Neural Networks and Kalman Filters for Energy Management Systems
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) concepts are widely used for controlling and managing electrical power, especially for residential and commercial buildings. However, these controls are still condition-based methods that are limited in decision-making and inflexible operation. In addition, the transmission of data from sensors over the internet may be interrupted or scrambled, resulting in a controller processing error. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-based approach for controlling IoT devices to enhance the ability of the controller to operate intelligently. A neural network technique is used to optimize the controller operation in the IoT system. The state estimation approach using the Kalman filter (KF) algorithm is proposed to reduce data errors and increase the reliability of the IoT control system. The proposed intelligent IoT approach is implemented for energy management and tested on a laboratory case study to minimize energy use for the lighting system. The experimental results show that the proposed method decreases 49.56% of electricity consumption and reduces the data variance from sensors by 77.13% compared to the conventional system without intelligent control. The test results indicate that integrating AI and KF with the IoT system can efficiently and effectively control and manage the lighting system.

articleTitle: An Analysis Software Utilizing Thermal Image, Emissivity Calibration and Maintenance Rules
abstract: The objective of this work was to implement a software to utilize available thermal images and maintenance rules in order to classify the urgency of maintenance action in electrical distribution systems. To achieve such purpose, the implemented software consists of two parts. The first part analyzes and calibrates the true temperature of a pixel of interest in the thermal image. The software can also compare temperatures between any two pixels in the thermal image. The assigned ambient temperature can be manually entered from a known value or selected from any pixel of the thermal image. The resulting calibrated temperature could be used to further evaluate the degree of maintenance required for abnormally heated electrical equipment. The second part determines the maintenance action timeline based on criteria guidelines. Both parts require a user with background knowledge of the corresponding electrical distribution system, such as type of material of the component or similar component in normal working condition necessary for comparison. The developed software had an average absolute error of only 1.70% in comparison with PCIRMeter and its features performed their functions as designed.

articleTitle: Powder Metallurgy Microstructure Classification Using Image Processing and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Evaluation of the fusion characteristic of the sintering neck is important to indicate the quality of metal workpieces forming with powder metallurgy. The quality is analyzed by microstructure images after forming. Currently, quality evaluation is primarily performed by experts without a clear standard; as a result, the goal of this study aims to present the application of image processing and deep learning based on the CNN (Convolution neural network) to develop a model to evaluate sintering neck using the characteristics of pores in microstructure images. Images evaluated by three metallurgical experts were utilized in a prototype for creating the deep learning model. The research measured the results of accuracy and time used in creating the model using five different algorithms. As the result, the accuracy range of 94-98% was obtained, except for the model generated by GoogLeNet which was unable to classify image types of pores, and ResNet-50 spent the shortest time constructing the deep learning model among all four models.

articleTitle: Minimizing Power Loss in a DC Distribution System through an Analysis of the Loss Sensitivity Factor and Distributed Generator Loss Characteristics
abstract: This paper presents a power loss reduction technique of DC distribution system by optimal location of DG based loss sensitivity factor and loss characteristic of DG capacity to search a best location and capacity of DG. The simulation result can be concluded that a loss sensitivity factor can be used for optimal DG placement and loss characteristic of DG capacity can be calculated as an optimal capacity of DG at installed bus.

articleTitle: Realization of Lossy Parallel Inductance Simulator Using Single VDGA and a Grounded Capacitor
abstract: An active lossy parallel type inductance simulator is proposed in this study. Only a single voltage differencing gain amplifier (VDGA) and a grounded capacitor are used in the proposed design. The realized equivalent resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>) and equivalent inductance (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>) can be adjusted electronically via the transconductance gain of the VDGA device. The influence of the non-idealities of the VDGA on the realized simulator is examined in detail. The suggested active inductance simulator is used to realize the second order voltage mode highpass filter, which is simulated using the PSPICE simulation program to ensure that it performs as expected.

articleTitle: The effect of solid cylindrical rod diameter and pulse electric current of joule heating for flash graphene methodology from graphite
abstract: This paper reports on the effect of solid cylindrical rod diameter and pulse electric current on joule heating for flash graphene methodology from graphite using a finite element method. Thermal and heat flux distribution of graphite rod cells were carefully analyzed and simulated by three-dimensional finite element modeling. Interestingly it was found that the diameter of the graphite and the pulse electric current affected the temperature generation occurring within the graphite. The temperature at the middle point of the graphite was approximately 8.46 % higher than the graphite-copper junction.

articleTitle: Effect of Rear Irradiance on Series and Shunt Resistance of n-Type PERT Bifacial Silicon Module
abstract: The purpose of this research is to determine the Bifaciality parameter and to study the variation of series and shunt resistance by the Single IV Curve method and refer to the IEC TS 60904-1-2 2019 standard for the experimental. The results showed that Bifaciality had an effect on the increase in power. Bifaciality was between 78.51%-83.20%, with Pmax lower than Isc by 4.7%, but within the normal range of n-Type PERT modules. Bifaciality increases the total absorbance used to produce energy and affects the current-voltage characteristic, thereby changing the series and shunt resistances. From the experiment, it was found that the series resistance (Rs) decreases, and the shunt resistance (Rsh) increases as the incident light increases.

articleTitle: Intelligent Learning Control System via Unfalsified Control
abstract: In this paper, we present an intelligent learning algorithm via unfalsified control. Using this approach, the algorithm can distinguish quality of candidate controllers by experimental plant input and output data. The key is at how to compute the new fictitious error signal. Any artificial intelligence technique can be applied using the proposed concept. Finally, we discuss an open problem whether or not the algorithm can achieve human intelligence.

articleTitle: Comparison of LFP battery performance between Screw welding and Laser beam welding
abstract: Studying the comparison of the performance of battery packing between screw welding technique and laser beam welding technique, both battery packing techniques have different advantages and disadvantages to different manufacture and assembling. The research is testing the performance of using battery packing in both techniques by choosing the Lithium iron phosphate(LFP) battery manufactured and distributed in the present market. This research will compare the life cycle testing, which tests the battery life performance, testing DC internal resistance of the battery, and comparing the battery's temperature increase while the battery discharged. To collect the performance testing data and choose the most suitable for application use with suitable battery packing technique.

articleTitle: “Patiyoot” Cryptography Authentication Protocol for Computer Network
abstract: Authentication is the process of identifying users that request access to a system, network, or device. It keeps invalid users out of databases, networks, and other resources. It is a system for differentiating legitimate users from illegitimate ones. If a message is not original and timely, then it is considered as not being authentic, not being from whom it claims to be. An authentication protocol is defined as a computer system communication protocol which may be encrypted and designed specially to securely transfer authenticated data between two parties. In this research paper, the new of authentication protocol called "Patiyoot" is invented and explained. It consists of ten steps. Each step is elaborated with the reason why it is done in that particular way. It enhances security from the previous conventional authentication protocols, which have some security issues, by using Nonce and Timestamp.

articleTitle: Design of PV system for a Primary Distribution System under Loss and Voltage Drop Control Based on ETAP
abstract: This paper presents a design of a PV system for a primary distribution system under loss and voltage drop control based on ETAP program. The research area is selected within Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi (RMUTT), Thailand. The Power System Simulator (ETAP) is used to design a primary distribution system simulation and PV installed of the RMUTT electrical system. The simulation results by comparing the loss and voltage drop from the based case and PV system installed of 900 kWp can be presented by reducing the grid’s electrical power loss and voltage drop.

articleTitle: Study of Distributed Temperature Sensing and Applications
abstract: This paper shows Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS) technology and system implementation. Raman scattering is applied to this DTS system. The innovation and system implementation are explained in this paper. This also includes monitoring system working with optical fiber sensors. The software is developed by using LabVIEW for measuring temperature and this can be applied to various applications.

articleTitle: A Position Control System for a Single-port Laparoscopic Manipulating Robot
abstract: The research herein proposes a position control system, designed for a single-port surgical robot, based on the lockup table method. The programmable logic controller (PLC) was implemented to move the single- port surgical robot and handle laparoscope and surgical instruments with feedback control. The output responses of the desired angle were investigated under several conditions. The rotating angle allows movement of the laparoscope in the range of -10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> to +10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. The error of the desired position of the designed system was less than approximately ± 0.1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. Moreover, the output data from several experiments may be employed to improve the open-loop control systems. This system is also capable of providing computer vision task implementation, enabling semi- automatic or automatic surgery in the future.

articleTitle: Deep learning-based monitoring system for distress on mice using behavior analysis
abstract: Experiments in medical laboratories are required to strictly follow several ethical and legal regulations as they involve utilizing animals in research. These requirements aim to relieve and minimize the suffering from used animals. Many studies and research were proposed to find efficient methods to detect and measure the distress level in animals. However, they are still labor-intensive and require a lot of manual effort. Especially, there is no published artificial system that allows detecting distress and pain in mice based on their behaviors. In this work, we propose an automatic monitoring system of mouse activity that targets to process raw videos with the standard set-up to examine the pain/distress symptoms through mouse behaviors. We make use of recent deep learning advances in object detection and action recognition field to allow detecting animals in boxes and analyzing their behaviors. The result showed that the proposed automated monitoring system is efficient in recognizing mouse behavior and can be used to early identify the sign of pain in mice.

articleTitle: Improve a Voltage Unbalance Index of Bipolar DC Distribution Grid By using Particle Swarm Optimization Based on Load Balancing Method
abstract: This paper presents a bipolar DC distribution grid power flow model and load balancing method by using particle swarm optimization (PSO) to reduce power loss due to neutral current and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) due to unbalance load at each bus. The objective function leads to reducing neutral current by transferring load at each bus to balance a load at each pole by considering the various condition. The results lead to conclude that the load balancing method can be reduced neutral current, reduce power loss and improve the VUF of a modified IEEE 69 bus system.

articleTitle: Effect of Resampling Techniques on Deep Learning Model Training in Sleep Apnea Classification
abstract: This study is using deep learning model to classify the respiratory events of Sleep Disordered Breathing (SDB) data. Our pilot results showed the missed identification in some classes even the total accuracy is high. This is the result of unbalanced training dataset given to the model. Two different resampling techniques; Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and Random Under-Sampling (RUS), were introduced to balance the data. One hundred overnight nasal airflow signals were randomly selected from NIH funded polysomnography database. They were used to train and test these two algorithms with Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model. The results showed greater agreement index when compared between with and without data resampling process. However, SMOTE in sum performed better than RUS (93.72% vs 70.01% in overall accuracy and 0.91 vs 0.55 in Cohen’s kappa). It demonstrates that the over-sampling technique is more powerful than under-sampling one. Other resampling techniques will be investigated to make the robust conclusion.

articleTitle: Wind farm selection and transmission line expansion planning based on the portfolio theory
abstract: The sites of a wind farms and transmission lines should be selected effectively during the planning of large-scale wind power generators. In this study, the sites of wind farms were selected by a portfolio selection method and transmission line expansions were optimized by a genetic algorithm. The portfolio selection method was used to determine the minimum risk for the generated power, and a genetic algorithm was used to further optimize the cost consideration. The proposed methods were able to find the appropriate wind farm locations that maximized the power generation at the minimal transmission expansion cost.

articleTitle: Planar Electrode Probe Patterns for Cervical Precancerous Screening using Electrical Impedance Tomography
abstract: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of death for many women around the world. In this paper, study and design electrode probe along with using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) method to find the most efficient electrode probe for cervical precancerous tissues screening. Two types of planar electrodes probe with 7 or 8 electrodes were investigated by simulation: circular and square layouts. The circular layout has 4 mm diameter and the square layout has 4 mm side length. The simulation result showed that the circular 7-electrode was most suitable for localizing cervical precancerous tissues with the localization error less than 1.7mm. The signal-to-noise ratio should be over 40dB and the current patterns should be designed with symmetrical patterns. The region beneath electrodes, however, still be blind spots to detect abnormality.

articleTitle: Rank Reversal Effect on Multicriteria Ranking for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing under Shadowing and Noise Uncertainty
abstract: Rank reversal is the main challenge of multi-criteria ranking method. Currently, CSS adopts the multi-criteria ranking to determine the quality of SUs. However, the effect of rank reversal to the performance of CSSs based on multi-criteria ranking have not been investigated yet. Therefore, in this paper, we evaluate the rank reversal effect on the performance of CSSs based on multi-criteria ranking under poor environment such noise uncertainty and shadowing effect. As a result, AMT can avoid the rank reversal occurrence and presents rank reversal robustness under decision threshold adapting strategy. On the other hand, based on fixed threshold, AMR suffers from rank reversal. Moreover, we compare the performance of AMR and AMT to IMA and K-of-N under different number of SUs. It can be noticed that AMT and IMA do not suffer from the number of SUs by determining the optimal number of SUs to determine the channel availability. On the contrary, the performance of K-of-N and AMR degrade under an increasing in the number of SUs once the unreliable SUs are taken into the account in order to determine the channel availability.

articleTitle: The Electrical Characteristics of Pencils Affecting the Human Body
abstract: This research study the effect of pencil electrical characteristic to human body. The resistance, resistivity and conductivity are parameters for testing the 10 types of pencil. By the length of pencil separated 3 parts for measuring are 5cm, 10cm and 15cm. and final part for testing is used the 15cm of pencil connect to the standard human body (SHB) circuit for measure the current flow though pencil in 2 conditions were the SHB circuit with moisture and without moisture. From result found that the resistance and conductivity have maximum values were 91Ω and 35758 S/m at 4H and 5B types of pencil respectively. Then, the maximum resistivity was 2.88 mΩ/m at the 4H of pencil. The current values of pencil on the SHB circuit with moisture has maximum about 370 mA to 385 mA at the 4H to 5B types of pencil. Conclusion, the most effect from electrical characteristic of pencil to human body was the SHB with moisture condition because the current level of results has the dangerous to human body in zone 5.

Author Keywords: effect of AC current on human body

articleTitle: Channel Estimation Based On Pilot Signal and Iterative Method for TDD Based Massive MIMO Systems
abstract: This paper applies an iterative method to low computational complexity LS algorithm. An orthogonality property obtained from Hadamard code utilizes with pilot signal to identify base stations in cellular networks. These techniques are used to estimate channel state information and mitigates the effect of full pilot contamination or full pilot reuse in TDD based massive MIMO systems. Simulation results show that performance of an achievable downlink rate (b/s/Hz) obtained from the proposed technique is higher than that of both the LS algorithm with and without base station identity codes in time-varying fading channel.

articleTitle: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Universal Filter Using DDTAs
abstract: This paper presents a multiple-input multiple-output universal biquadratic filter using differential difference transconductance amplifiers. The variant filtering responses can be obtained by appropriately applying input signals and appropriately choosing output terminals. The voltage-mode filter possesses both high-input and low-output impedances. The proposed filter provides five standard filtering responses. The natural frequency can be controlled electronically, and the quality factor can be controlled orthogonally. The performance of the proposed filter is confirmed using PSPICE simulation based on 0.18 μm CMOS technology from TSMC.

articleTitle: Investigation of Screening Filter Methods to Enhance Computation Speed of Conjunction Assessment Analysis
abstract: The collision events in space result in generating a large number of fragmentation debris in orbit that threats to active satellites or spacecraft in near future. Currently, the space traffic management system analyzes the conjunction assessment to evaluate the collision risk of satellite by defining the time closest approach (TCA) and miss distance between two space objects to decide the collision avoidance maneuver plan of satellite when there is a high chance of collision. However, the computation time of conjunction analysis is the key to decide the collision maneuver plan to mitigate the collision risks because the conjunction analysis assessment algorithm without a filter spend huge runtime to detect the TCA of all space objects. In order to enhance the computation speed, the conjunction filter algorithms are very useful for finding the conjunction events of some objects before computing the precise TCA and miss distance. The timestep analysis is one of the keys to increase the computation speed. However, the filter possible miss some conjunction events. This paper presents the investigations of two conjunction filter methods: "Smart Sieve" and "CSieve" to define the conjunction events of three Thai satellites: THEOS, NAPA-1 and NAPA-2 by varying the timestep of both filters. The analyzed results (computation cost, number of conjunction events) are compared with the conjunction assessment analysis without filter.

articleTitle: Improvement of Self-Heating in Quantum Dot Reflective Semiconductor Optical Amplifier for SS-OCT Application
abstract: In this study, with the application to SS-OCT in mind, the effect of self-heating generated in QD-RSOA was examined by the simulation analysis in order to realize the heterogeneous integration wavelength-variable laser which can sweep the wavelength at high speed with narrow line width, and improvement of the heat radiation property were examined. It was clarified that the heat radiation property can be efficiently improved by thinning the substrate and mounting the p-electrode side toward the chip carrier (submount). It was also shown that the active layer temperature can be suppressed to 97 ℃ at the maximum under the current density of 25 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by adopting the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> window structure rather than the BCB embedded structure. And, the characteristic improvement of QD-RSOA was examined by evaluating the saturated optical output power of the QD-LD. The saturated optical output power was compared between the p-side up and down structures in the QD-LD of the BCB embedded structure, and it was possible to obtain approximately twice higher output power in the p-side down structure than that in the p-side up mount structure.

articleTitle: An Application of an Adaptive Signal Processing Scheme for a QPSK Signal Demodulation
abstract: An adaptive digital signal processing scheme applied for a digital communication has been presented in the press. The model of an ANC is utilized to demodulate in a coherent detection scheme for a received QPSK signal. The coefficients of the system will be updated by the least mean square (LMS) algorithm that is controlled in the adaptation sequence according to the symbol duration of the received signal. Since such a manner is performed, the system is similar to integrate and dump (I&D) correlator in behavior. The analysis and simulation results have implied that the desired information signal can be recovered from the received signal by the proposed scheme with the same performance as the conventional optimum demodulation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Fuzzy Logic Controller for Oxygen Control System in Aquaculture Pond
abstract: The objective of this research is to implementation of fuzzy logic controller system for monitoring the water quality of aquaculture ponds by monitoring the temperature and dissolved oxygen. The measured water quality level decides when to turn the pump ON/OFF. The proposed system is straightforward to use for aquaculture farmers. Experimental results show that fuzzy logic controllers used to control water oxygen systems can reduce the electricity consumption of the pumps ON/OFF and reduce the risk of mortality in aquaculture effectively.

articleTitle: Mixed-Mode Universal Filter using MCDCTA and Grounded Capacitors
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a mixed-mode (MM) universal filter that realizes generic filter functions in all two possible modes, namely current-mode (CM) and transimpedance-mode (TIM). The structure of the filter circuit consists of one multifunction current differencing cascaded transconductance amplifier (MCDCTA) and only two grounded capacitors which is ideally suited for IC fabrication. It can be provided with low-pass (LP), band-pass (BP), and high-pass (HP) responses in both CM and TIM without changing the circuit structure. Additionally, the CM is very well known for its low input impedance and high output impedance, which makes it a perfect design. In both modes, the pole frequency and quality factor can be electronically adjusted. The proposed circuit was validated by simulation of the PSpice program, consistent with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Temperature Distribution from The Comparison Egg Incubator Shape by 3-D Finite Element Method
abstract: Arithmetical model of temperature in the egg incubator which are manifested in the second-order partial differential equation is introduced in this paper. MATLAB program with 3-D finite element method in a programmatic simulation was applied for temperature examination. The egg incubator analysis. According to the simulation model of the egg incubator in the shape of curve, hexagon, and square, it is found that the temperature distribution of curve egg incubator is the best distributed by consider standard deviation that is less than other shape, there were on steady-state at 37 °C at 20 minutes.

Author Keywords: computer simulation 3-D finite element method (3-D FEM)

articleTitle: The six electric fault zone analysis for predictive maintenance on motors of the continuous production
abstract: This paper proposes for motor health analysis by classifying into six fault zones. These consist of power quality, power circuit, insulation, stator, rotor, and air gap. First of all, power quality would consider on the quantity between voltage and current. Secondly, power current plays a role on the current supplied to the motor. Thirdly, insulation would take a focus on insulation’s health among windings and ground. Fourth, stator condition concerns insulation of windings, solder joints between the coils and the stator core. Fifth, rotor focuses on the condition of both rotor cage and lamination. Lastly, air gap would mainly concern concentricity between rotor and stator. All of these fault zones would be diagnosed for condition-based monitoring with the aims to prevent any premature damage on motor and also to saves maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Application of port-Hamiltonian Approach in Controller Design for Buck Boost Converter
abstract: Controlling output voltage of the DC-DC Buck-Boost converter has been a challenging topic for many years, since its averaged dynamics is a non-minimum phase system with highly load variation. Several methods avoid this difficulty by controlling the voltage via the inductor current. This paper presents a nonlinear energy-based controller design approach, which can directly control the output voltage without internal current loop. Due to damping assignment technique, the damping of the closed-loop system can be determined, and the problem with load variation is solved. To verify the performance of the proposed approach, the controller is test with a simulation and with existing converter. The result confirms the achievement of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: 3-D Morphological Analysis of Line-Shaped Particle from Digital In-line Holograms
abstract: A new digital-holographic method for analyzing 3-D surface morphology of particles is proposed. The proposed method does not only solve an inherent limitation of conventional imaging systems in preserving depth information of 3-D objects, but also has an advantage over the previous works in that it provides exact particle information and constructs 3-D surface morphology with reality sense. Experimental verifications of the proposed method are done by using a 100 μm polycarbonate microtube.

articleTitle: Forecasting SF6 Emission from High Voltage System with Data Mining
abstract: This research focused on which factors affect SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> emission based on the UN database by using a data mining method. We selected two suitable methods: linear regression and decision tree classification. The interested factors may affect SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> emission include electricity installed capacity, GDP, import and export of parts of semiconductor devices, import and export of electrical insulator, import and export of magnesium unwrought, population density, and per capita electricity consumption. We found that installed capacity is one of the most effective factors to SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> emission from linear regression as well as total parts of semiconductor devices and similar devices trade is the most distinction as a root node from decision tree classification. Linear regression model comes with a large relative error in this case, while the classification method provides much better accuracy.

articleTitle: Needs assessment and prototype of a low-cost radiation monitoring system for citizens in Fukushima
abstract: Based on a questionnaire survey of approximately 1,500 child-rearing people living in Fukushima Prefecture, we developed a prototype of a new radiation visualization system required by citizens. The demonstration test results confirm that the system works properly in high-dose areas in Fukushima Prefecture. The system is expected to provide local residents with a quantitative monitoring of natural decay and decontamination results and reassurance that they can return to their original land and live in peace.

articleTitle: Switching Current-Voltage of memristor with double barriers Schottky diode
abstract: This research is purpose on the memristor device investigated on nanoscale technology in which an expressed the fundamental circuit of the fourth-order element. The theoretical memristor expression of the missing link between electric charge and flux linkage represent, which was proposed by Chua in 1971. In the process is the procedure of fabrication technology by using TiO2 on thin-film of memristor device, the structure compounded with the dopant atoms are doped region and an undoped region. This research is investigated the Schottky diode on the planar metal-semiconductor-metal structure with wide electrodes separations of 2D2R device. The characteristics of the current-voltage relation introduce the device behavior of memristance with the effect of a pinched hysteresis loop that depends on the frequency and magnitude of the voltage. Under applied a few voltages across two electrodes device, it's causing a high electric field to represent the high resistive state and low resistive state. As described in the result of the experiment, the carrier charge and flux linkage have crossed the boundary between the depleted region and the neutral silicon region by a high electric switching.

articleTitle: Lung Volume Estimation based on Bioimpedance Measurement and Neural Network
abstract: Lung volume is an indicator used for evaluating how healthy of lungs are. Apart from using expensive equipment, lung volume can be determined by bioimpedance obtained by measuring at several regions around the chest. The bioimpedance values are usually used by the Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) technique, which transforms the several bioimpedance values into an image of conductivity distribution. EIT is inexpensive and can be used to monitor lungs in real-time. However, EIT is computation expensive and cannot provide the lung volume directly. In this study, the neural network technique was used to estimate the left- and the right-lung volume by using the bioimpedance values as used in EIT. Two network architectures were investigated by simulation. The result shows that neural networks can efficiently estimate lung volumes with the error of less than 0.78 ml and with a correlation of higher than 0.99. Even adding noise to the degree of 40 dB signal-to-noise ratio, the performance was still satisfactory. Two-layer network architecture was also sufficient for this lung application.

articleTitle: Design of Cooling System of Tier 3 Standard for Rack Enclosure in the Containerized Data Centers
abstract: The purpose study was to illustrate how the function of the designed tier 3 standard for rack enclosure in the containerized data centers (Containerized DC) with Thailand data center standards. Our results of the design show that containerized data centers achieve 95% and 60% savings in the cooling system in containers and facility powers respectively compared to a building data center and that savings of 60% in cooling power are possible when workloads are consolidated onto the least number of containers. We also show that the new cooling system optimizations technique is very effective at high utilization and that this data center can approach the efficiency of a container at high utilizations when employing a simple cooling optimization.

articleTitle: Economic and Sensitivity Analyses for an Optimal Hybrid Power Generation for Stand-Alone Power Systems: Case of Klongrua, Phato, Chumphon, Thailand
abstract: This paper analyzes a hybrid power system for an independent power system for Baan Khlongrua community, which is a village far from the transmission line system so that the community has electricity available all the time. The designed system consists of solar cells, batteries, inverters and small power turbines. Therefore, this research assesses the economic value and analyzes the system's sensitivity. It is assumed that the electricity demand will increase by 4.25% per year. The analysis data found that in the first year, the cost of energy (COE) was 0.137 $/kWh, the second year was 0.132 $/kWh, and the third year was 0.127 $/kWh. Year 1 has a high COE due to system design being approximately 10% larger than current demand, and in years 4, 5, 6, COE will increase. As a result of the designed system, it will not produce enough electricity to meet the electrical load of the village. Therefore, a diesel generator compensates during the power shortage, causing the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> value in the year 4,5,6 to 3,780 kg/yr 2,898 kg/yr 3,265 kg/yr increased. This CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> value, therefore, affects the COE increase, and COE decreases from 0.137 to 0.127 $/kWh. the payback period of the system can be quickly achieved.

articleTitle: An energy-effective altitude controller of a pusher-type hybrid UAV in transition phases
abstract: Recent decades have witnessed an increasing interest in QuadPlane UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles) thanks to its automatic ability in vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) without a pilot and a runway. However, pusher-type QuadPlane UAVs show a disadvantage in the sense of maintaining a useless payload (quad motors) during the flight time; that is, the quad motors are only used about 5 minutes in only VTOL phases while a flight time is usually about 3 hours. Reducing the quad rotors' weight requires an energy-effective altitude control law, which also plays an essential role in guaranteeing flight safety because there is redundant energy to deal with an emergency. This paper introduces an energy-effective altitude control law for a pusher-type QuadPlane UAV in transition phases based on the sliding mode control technique. The proposed control law estimates the aerodynamic force in the longitude channel to reduce required quad energy based on UAV state and aerodynamic coefficients. Simulation and actual flight test results show that the proposed control law is better than the standard PID controller in terms of altitude tracking errors (about four times) and energy (about 1.5 times).

articleTitle: Single MCDCTA Based Current-mode Multiphase Sinusoidal Oscillator
abstract: The multiphase sinusoidal oscillator is proposed in this article. A single multifunction current differencing cascaded transconductance amplifier (MCDCTA), three resistors, and three capacitors are used in the proposed circuit with high-output-impedance nodes. The proposed circuit can be operated by electronic adjusting the oscillation condition without affecting the oscillation frequency. The proposed circuit was verified via a computer simulation that is agreed to the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: IPPs Daily Optimal Operation Considering of Generation’s Output Responsiveness
abstract: Modern technology in the service of modern operation theory is more than adequate to provide effective operation to meet the needs of any possible new structure or structures. This paper assumes that ISO (Independent System Operator) will give the next day's power purchase fee, then proposes a new effective and simple methodology for solving the IPP daily optimal operation model. The proposed operation model and optimal methods consider not only the profit/loss value of power purchase fee but also the dynamic load response constraint of the generators. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simple case simulations.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Air-Clad Type Silicon-Nitride Ring-Resonator for Bio-Sensing Applications
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency silicon nitride (SiN) based air-clad type ring resonator that sandwiched with air cladding and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> cladding for silicon photonic (SiPh) device was demonstrated. The simulation results showed that 400 nm-thick SiN waveguide have maximum coupling efficiency with a coupling loss of 7.2 dB. By using CMOS compatible process with single lithography (stepper) and reactive ion etching step, high qualities SiN waveguide was fabricated without silicon wafer warpage. The optical output characteristics of ring resonators with the free spectral range of 3.9 nm were obtained. This device can detect NaCl concentrations of 50-1000 mMole in deionized water. Therefore, SiN waveguide grating coupler is one of a promising SiPh devices for bio-sensing applications.

articleTitle: The Fuzzy Controller for a Boost Derived - Hybrid Converter
abstract: This paper proposes the design of fuzzy controller for a boost derived-hybrid converter (BDHC) to control the output voltage for DC loads and AC loads at the desired constant levels. From a single dc source, the BDHC can generate both dc and ac loads at a same time. The fuzzy controller is designed for the BDHC to obtain good performance in under transient and steady states. The proposed fuzzy controller is based on the investigation of converter behavior to generate the appropriate fuzzy rules. The output voltage error and the input current error are considered as the input membership functions and whereas the output membership function is the control signal. After the defuzzification, the control signal is used for pulse width modulation in order to provide the required switching signals for all four switches of the BDHC. Simulation results show the satisfactory performance of the proposed fuzzy controller for the regulation of the converter output voltage under various operating situations

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Net-Zero Energy Buildings with Hybrid Energy Sources
abstract: Designing and analyzing a net-zero energy building (NZEB) integrated with multiple energy sources to reduce annual energy costs and promote renewable energy utilization is a complicated work process. This paper proposes a new design methodology for NZEB that utilizes the energy sources from electricity grids, photovoltaic (PV), and battery energy storage systems. The design algorithm is divided into five steps: building data collection, energy management, optimum PV and battery sizing, energy analysis, and financial evaluation. NZEB energy analysis is performed using the building's data and the design energy sources to determine the net annual energy value conducted with PVsyst software. The proposed approach is applied to renovate a four-floor university building with an area of 2,248 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is used as a case study. The comparative studies and simulation results show that the proposed method provides optimal PV and battery sizes to effectively transform the conventional building into NZEB in both on-grid and off-grid connections.

articleTitle: Regenerative Battery Charging Control for PMDC Motor Using a Modulus Counter Switching Technique
abstract: This paper presents a simulation of the charging of lithium-ion batteries and super capacitors for electric vehicles (EV). The charging current of both devices is controlled by a hysteresis circuit to maintain a constant current in The hybrid battery charge is shown programmatically. MATLAB/Simulink. The modulus counter is used to control the pulse signal to the boost buck converter which is charged by the permanent magnet DC motor. This is like regenerative breaking to charge both energy storage devices. The simulation results show the energy storage efficiency shown by the charging time values from the MATLAB-Simulink program.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Steady-state, Pulse, and Programmable of Tungsten Halogen Solar Simulator
abstract: The steady-state and pulse solar simulators were the light source to measure the current-voltage characteristics of the photovoltaic (PV) cell or panel or test for the hot spot endurance test according to the IEC 61215 and the IEC 61646 standards. The programmable solar array simulator tests the PV system, but it is high cost. The programmable solar simulator is the choice for the lower price. This paper presents the low-cost programmable tungsten solar simulator with 8.0% non-uniformity 3.0% steady-state temporal instability. The test plane irradiance was according to the reference with a correlation coefficient of 0.95.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Six-Port Reflectometer Technique for Quality Determination of Para Rubber Latex
abstract: This paper presents a dual-frequency six-port reflectometer (SPR) applied to determine dry rubber content (DRC) in para rubber latex. The SPR consists of a wideband microwave source, a six-port ring circuit, a tunable matching circuit, and a microcontroller unit. Two stable frequencies at 1 and 2.16 GHz are proposed for sensing dry rubber content in para rubber latex under test. Several samples of 20-60% DRC concentrated para rubber latex are measured at both frequencies under the temperature range of 20 - 45°C. These data sets are prepared for training and testing for obtaining a temperature-independent model for DRC determination. Three machine learning algorithms, Bayesian Regularization algorithm (BRA), Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMA), and Scaled Conjugate Gradient (SCG), are applied for model training. Based on the experiment data sets, the BRA yields 0.157 mean square error for training and 0.163 for testing while the regression values for training and testing are 0.999.

articleTitle: An Air Force Cooling of Lithium–ion Battery Thermal Management System for Heat Eliminating in Modified Electric Vehicle
abstract: This paper proposes the technique of modified minivan vehicle from Internal combustion Engine (ICE) to electric vehicle. The main equipment composed of 30 kW motor with converter and 16.92 kWh of NMC battery are calculated from weight and velocity requirement. The battery packing and heat generation evaluation by using principle of thermodynamic law and simulation model with solid works is illustrated. The air flow cooling system which consisted of 6 fans of 150 cubic feet/min, total flow is about 900 cubic feet/min are installed and experimented by operate the load at 70, 174 and 200 A respectively. The temperature increasing form heat generation of three case are 34, 60 and 72 Celsius. The protection system is determined for control the temperature within 60 degree for prevent thermal runaway.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Harnessing an Urban Wind Turbine to Supply an Electric Motorbike in Thailand
abstract: This paper presents a feasibility study of the employment of a wind turbine to supply an electric motorbike in the urban area. The turbine investigated was selected based upon three dimensional numerical simulations. The turbine annual energy production (AEP) was evaluated using measured wind data which is in the form of Weibull distribution. The feasibility of the system was determined in terms of number of charges for a 1 kW motorbike. The effects the variation of the Weibull distribution was also studied. It is found that the AEP is most sensitive to the scale factor. From all investigated cases, The Weibull distribution with a shape factor of 1.9 and a scale factor of 5 provides the maximum AEP of 2,950 kWh or a total number of 2,458 charges a year.

articleTitle: Exploration of Sub-Optimal Constellation Maps for Coherent Fiber-Optic Communication links by Auto-Encoder Type Machine Learning
abstract: Autoencoder (AE) was applied to the exploration of sub-optimal constellation maps and decision boundaries in a coherent optical fiber communication link. Single-wavelength point-to-point single-mode fiber coherent optical communication link that considers wavelength dispersion and self-phase modulation was incorporated in the middle of AE and sub-optimal constellation maps / decision boundaries were automatically acquired by learning AE under various conditions. The transmitting side of AE automatically configured an encoder, so called AE modulation (AEM), from one-hot-vectors to IQ constellations considering noise, wavelength dispersion, and self-phase modulation (SPM) given during transmission, and the receiving side automatically configured a decoder having linear decision boundaries from the received IQ constellations to one-hot vectors. Setting an appropriate signal-to-noise power ratio (SNR) during AE learning resulted in constellations and decision boundaries stable for wide range of operating SNR. The obtained BER characteristic for 16AEM was approaching to the one of the compensated 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (16QAM).

articleTitle: Preliminary Design on Modular Electrical Autonomous Vehicle
abstract: Automation has been used in many industrial applications, such as process in any factory which includes the inventory management of products. Autonomous vehicle can help with inventory management by deliver inventories to its desired destination. Electric vehicle (EV) has less complexity of engines and pollution free comparing to internal combustion engine vehicle. Modular design leads trend of using this system in the factory as it is simple to scale up the size and quantity of the system. Lidar with computer vision (line tracking) is used to compute the robot localization, path planning and obstacle avoidance which integrate with Robot Operating System (ROS). This paper describes the Modular Electric Autonomous Vehicle (MEAV) is study and designed and tested in the real factory.

articleTitle: Diffusion Mixed-Node Recursive Least Square-based Algorithm over Adaptive Network
abstract: This paper proposes a diffusion framework related on the mixed-node constraint based on recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm with adaptive network. The proposed Combine-Then-Adapt and Adapt-Then-Combine diffusion algorithms based on RLS algorithm are derived shortly by minimising the mixed-node least square-based criterion for distributed estimation over the adaptive network. The mixed-node cost function is described and illustrated briefly. Experimental results depict that these proposed algorithms is able to achieve the fast convergence better than the conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: An Accelerated Nonparametric Bayesian Approach for Anomaly Detection with Feature Selection
abstract: This paper proposes an accelerated variational approach for learning infinite generalized inverted Dirichlet mixture to deal concurrently with two challenging problems: clustering and feature weighting. The statistical framework considers a Dirichlet process (DP) prior for the generalized inverted Dirichlet (GID) that has proven to be efficient for the clustering of semi-bounded data. In high dimensional spaces, the selection of the most informative and relevant features has an important role in terms of clustering accuracy and thus we include feature weighting to emphasize relevant features. An application that concerns anomaly detection indicates the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: The Analysis Harmonic for Connect Grid Photovoltaic Rooftop Synergy Distribution System
abstract: This paper presents the harmonic analysis for connecting grid photovoltaic rooftop synergy distribution system. The harmonic of photovoltaic rooftop affects the power distribution system’s power quality. Under limitations, it has technical impacts such as unbalanced current, flicker, and load in the photovoltaic rooftop system. Therefore, this paper is presented to analyze the harmonics problem in the power distribution system from the photovoltaic rooftop by measuring unbalanced current, flicker, and harmonic photovoltaic rooftop synergy distribution system. The results showed that measurement points at the point of common coupling (PCC) between photovoltaic rooftop and distribution system could analyze the distribution system’s harmonics.

articleTitle: Classification of Angle of Eye Movement using Electrooculography with LED testing sphere
abstract: This paper proposed the classification of the direction and degree of eye movements using EOG signals 2 channels based on discrete cosine transform and power of discrete signal. The EOG signal collect from the electrode placed on the around of eye in vertical and horizontal and using LED testing sphere to guide the EOG signal from the eye muscles. The k-means Clustering used to identify the posture and degree of eye view. The results show that this method can identify four motion gestures: up sight, down sight, left sight and right sight, with an average accuracy of 98.57% and can distinguish the five degrees of view: 5°, 10°, 15°, 20° and 25° with an average accuracy of 91.94%.

articleTitle: An Experiment approach of Low Radiation Energy Management for Photovoltaic Pumping system
abstract: In this paper purposes the management low radiation energy for Photovoltaic (PV) pumping system. The system consists of PV 300 Watt panel, a 24V 300W centrifugal pump, a 24V 12Ah lithium-ion phosphate battery and 24V 30A pulse width modulate battery charge controller [1]. The Arduino and LabVIEW were chosen as function of parameters control to order on-off the relay and monitor display. The static head of pumping was set as 18 m about 50% of maximum static head of pump. The lithium-ion phosphate battery was design at depth of discharge, DOD, 50% [4]. Therefore, the experiment was setting up of 1) directly between the PV and the water pump or without control and 2) the PV pumping system between the PV and a lithium-ion phosphate battery for a water pump with a power management control system or with control. Therefore, with control experimental was reference to without control experiment parameter for switch the resource. The results shown that the specific energy of the direct coupling technique has a valve lower than control technique that means the system can be harvest the energy at low radiation and supplied to motor pump in the define time period [2]. The DOD is correlated with the design the sizing of the battery as well.

articleTitle: The Prediction of Lithium Battery Life in Cellular Telecommunication Stations
abstract: This research paper introduces the remaining useful life prediction of lithium batteries operating at 48 V, 100 Ah on the cellular telecommunication substation with the load supply current conditions 1C rate at 100% DOD. According to the prediction technique, a 100-cycle of experimental results of actual discharge time are used to create the equation by using the curve fitting technique. Finally, the obtained results can estimate the battery lifetime and identify the time which will be able to supply the battery's load if the battery is operated under any conditions.

articleTitle: Resistorless Transconductance-mode Multifunction Filter with Orthogonal and Electronic Tune of Natural Frequency and Quality Factor
abstract: This work provides the synthesis of multifunction biquad active filter which has three input voltage nodes and single output current node. The synthesis procedure which is based on the RLC parallel circuit is given step by step. An analog active building block employed in this synthesis is the modified current controlled current conveyor transconductance amplifier (M-CCCCTA). The proposed filtering structure consists of two M-CCCCTAs and two grounded capacitors without any passive resistors. All input voltage nodes and output current node are high impedance which is cascadable without the need of any buffer devices. Five second order filtering types are obtained in the network. The filtering parameters including the natural frequency (ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), quality factor (Q) and pass band gain are electronically controlled. In addition, the Q is also electronically controlled without disturbing the ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The PSpice simulations using the model process parameters of the NR100N (NPN) and PR100N (PNP) bipolar transistor arrays ALA400CBIC-R from AT&T are given to investigate the characteristics of the proposed active filter.

articleTitle: Application of Signed Quadrature Spatial Modulation in 6G Massive MIMO Systems
abstract: Regardless of the number of employing antennas, it has been proved that spatial modulation (SM) uses only a single radio frequency (RF) chain to perform digital signal processing in MIMO wireless communications. Therefore, spatial modulation can be used for realizing the 6G-MIMO systems, which are necessary to equip extremely massive numbers of antennas, since its unique property can completely satisfy energy efficiency, i.e., key performance metric for 6G mobile network. Unfortunately, it is quite difficult to attain “Terabit era” with SM because its spectral efficiency grows logarithmically with the number of transmitted antennas, e.g., just 14 bps/Hz from 1024×1024 16-QAM system. This motivates us to investigate the enhanced version of SM called signed quadrature spatial modulation (SQSM), which theoretically offers greater spectral efficiency. In order to exhibit its potential in 6G wireless system, the performances of such a technique under 6G parameters are primarily investigated in this work. Many research challenges regarding SQSM transmission for 6G systems are also addressed. Moreover, the normalization factor of SQSM is analyzed and generalized to facilitate the research in this field.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Force and Vibration Measurement Using FSR-402 and SW-420 Sensors for Sports Shoe Inspection
abstract: This paper presents a method of inspecting the dynamic responses of force and vibration affecting feet, heels, ankles, and knees of human subjects while walking and running with sports shoes. The sensor based (FSR and vibration) system was developed to inspect the effect of different shoe types on a dynamic response (force and vibration) of the human legs while walking and running. The experiment was carried out by using a microcontroller-based measurement of the forces through two kinds of sensing devices: an embedded system developed by using the force sensor (FSR-402), and vibration sensor (SW-420) to acquire foot contract forces and a vibration at the ankles and knees. The results showed a relative maximum error of 0.2%, with the forces affecting feet, heels, ankles, and knees while running at the speed of 15 km/hr. achieving 1.380 kN, 1.403 kN, 1.233 kN, and 1.345 kN, respectively. The potential of using such a proposed method for dynamic force evaluation for the design to support the dynamic force measurement of suitable shoes was investigated.
